_: Pack policy: recipes this pack gates behind a technology that Factorio leaves free. tools/gen_technologies.py merges these into the technology's own effect list. See docs/MAPPING.md.
_why: Factorio gates 150 of its 214 items and leaves ~60 free at the start. This pack has 19 recipes and every one of them is inside that free tier, so a faithful tree gates exactly two things and research feels disconnected from crafting. These entries put the pack's early machines behind Factorio's own early technologies instead.
_rule: Never invent a technology, and never move one. Only the effect list grows. The ids, costs, prerequisites and order stay Factorio's, so the tree is still the real one and each row here is deleted - not rewritten - the day the item Factorio actually gates arrives to take its place.
_seeds: What has to remain craftable with no research at all: the first lab, the science it eats, and the power to run it. gen_technologies.py takes the transitive ingredients of these and refuses to gate any of them, so this file cannot soft-lock a new world. Ore and stone are hand-mined in Minecraft, which is why no drill is a seed.

automation.note: Automation already unlocks the assembling machine and the long-handed inserter in Factorio. Adding the burner pair makes the first research the one that ends hand-feeding, which is what the word means - and it is reachable with ten red science, so it is the first thing a new world works towards.

electronics.note: The electric versions of the two above, behind the technology that is about electricity, at thirty red science with Automation as its prerequisite. That is the second step and the reason to keep researching.

logistics.note: Factorio's logistics technology is belts, splitters and chests. The wooden chest stays free - storage from the first minute is not negotiable - and the splitter and the fast inserter land here for free when they are built.
